project.name: EIR :: api
project.description:
The edge: an HTTP surface over eir-application's four entry points, and the operator page that drives them. This is what makes the engine a tool rather than a library — until now every control had a caller and no caller had a user.
NO ADR-0010 EXEMPTION, and that is a choice rather than an oversight. ADR-0010 exists so that a module which genuinely needs a framework can take one; this module does not. It serves five JSON endpoints and one page, which the JDK's own com.sun.net.httpserver covers, and it writes JSON by hand for the same reason RoutingTableFormat parses a routing table by hand — Jackson is banned in the calculation path and the format is small enough to own. Two things follow that are worth more here than the convenience: the whole repository still builds and runs with -o, so a bank's air-gapped CI needs no network, and there is no framework between an HTTP request and an invariant result.
What a production deployment changes, stated so nobody mistakes this for one: authentication and authorisation (there is none — FR-906's role model is unimplemented), TLS termination, the in-memory book replaced by eir-persistence's schema behind a real ContractStateSource, and eir-batch driving the population loop instead of a request thread. The seams for all four are the seven ports this module implements in memory.
Depends on eir-application and, through it, everything below. Nothing depends on this module.
